title: Terminate variant echo chain and strengthen decision telemetry
creator: Riley Chen
description: Summary: A capacity event on 2026-02-27 exposed a routing/fallback failure class where stale policy state + variant-tag mismatches produced an "echo chain" of reroutes across regions. The decision graph retried across decreasing-capacity variants and regions, causing amplified retries and a localized capacity burnout that impacted customers in EU-West and US-East for ~18 minutes. This ticket tracks the follow-up work to terminate echo chains deterministically and add decision-level telemetry and safeguards.
timeline:
2026-02-27 08:11 UTC - First elevated alerts: increased tail latency and 502s on hosted endpoints.
2026-02-27 08:14 UTC - Automatic policy fallback triggered to alternate variants/regions.
2026-02-27 08:18 UTC - Observed repeated cross-region reroutes (EU->US->EU) for several customer flows.
2026-02-27 08:25 UTC - Mitigation: emergency throttle on policy propagation and temporary sticky-route TTL increase.
2026-02-27 08:29 UTC - Service recovered to baseline after throttles and manual variant pinning.
Post-incident: root cause analysis identified race between policy mesh propagation and variant tagging + missing per-request decision hop limit, allowing a single request to be retried repeatedly across incompatible variants/regions.
root_cause: Three contributing factors: (1) policy propagation race: policy mesh updates were applied with eventual consistency and no monotonic versioning, leading to transient incompatible precedence across shards; (2) stale KV cache: router-side policy cache allowed decisions based on mismatched variant tags; (3) no per-request hop/cycle limit: the fallback logic had no explicit circuit to stop re-routing once a request looped between variants/regions.
mitigation_summary: Emergency mitigations (post-incident) included: throttling policy propagation, forcing a coordinated policy version sweep, increasing sticky-route TTLs for affected customers, and manual variant pinning for high-impact customers. These mitigations restored capacity but are not sustainable — permanent fixes are in this ticket.
action_items: Add hop/cycle circuit-breaker to routing decision path: enforce a configurable per-request max_hops (default=4) and surface when exceeded
Make policy propagation idempotent and monotonic: attach a version stamp to policy blobs and reject out-of-order applies
Invalidate router-side policy KV cache on version bump and expose TTL/last_applied_version metric
Add pre-fallback compatibility check: reject fallback to a variant if model flavor/profile is incompatible (sequence_length, kv-format, quantization) and count as terminal failure
Implement decision-hop telemetry: per-request hop_count, decision_trace (trimmed), and tagging of terminal_reason to trace logs
Add automatic short-circuit for observed cross-region echo patterns: if a request hits >2 regions within 10s, mark route as 'unstable' and use fallback policy with capacity-safety
Create a canary rollout plan for new propagation logic with per-shard ramp and automatic rollback on hop_spike metric
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer respects max_hops and returns terminal error without re-enqueuing when exceeded
Policy propagation includes monotonically increasing version stamp and rejects out-of-order applies in integration tests
KV cache exposes last_applied_version metric and a cache invalidation API; dashboards show version alignment across shards
Telemetry pipeline receives hop_count and a summarized decision_trace for at least 95% of sampled requests under load
E2E test that simulates propagation races no longer produces cross-region reroute loops in CI
runbook_changes: Add 'routing echo' scenario: detection criteria (hop_count > 3 across >1 region within 60s) and mitigation steps (throttle policy propagation, increase sticky TTL, pin variant) to SRE runbook
Document steps to force-policy-version-sweep using orchestration toolchain with idempotent apply command
Add immediate observability checklist: query hop_count histogram, regional skew, and last_applied_version diff
